message:
Hi Alex — I can help, but since it’s your final day we need to follow the break-glass/JIT access process to stay compliant.

Here’s what I need from you to proceed
- Ticket/approval: link to an approved ticket (manager or on-call lead sign-off) and requested access duration (e.g., 2–4 hours).
- Instance details: cloud/provider, project/subscription, VM name/ID, region/zone, OS, and whether there’s a bastion or Session Manager/OS Login enabled.
- Your SSH public key: prefer a fresh ed25519 key. If you don’t have one, generate:
  ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "alex@company" -f ~/.ssh/alex_staging_$(date +%Y%m%d) -N ''
  Send only the .pub content and its fingerprint:
  ssh-keygen -lf ~/.ssh/alex_staging_$(date +%Y%m%d).pub

Fastest compliant paths (I’ll execute one of these once approval and details are in place)
- AWS EC2 (preferred: Session Manager)
  1) Open SSM session to the instance.
  2) Add your key:
     sudo useradd -m -s /bin/bash alex || true
     sudo mkdir -p -m 700 /home/alex/.ssh
     echo "ssh-ed25519 AAAA... alex@company" | sudo tee /home/alex/.ssh/authorized_keys >/dev/null
     sudo chown -R alex:alex /home/alex/.ssh
     sudo chmod 600 /home/alex/.ssh/authorized_keys
     sudo usermod -aG sudo alex
     sudo sed -i 's/^PasswordAuthentication .*/PasswordAuthentication no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config
     sudo systemctl reload ssh || sudo systemctl reload sshd
  3) Confirm Security Group allows SSH only from our bastion or your office IP.
  4) Time-box account or sudo to auto-expire at end of approved window.
  If SSM isn’t available: reboot with user data that adds your key, or attach root volume to a helper instance and inject the key offline.

- GCP Compute Engine
  - If OS Login is enabled: add your key to your user via IAM/OS Login.
  - If not: set instance/project metadata “ssh-keys” with:
    alex:ssh-ed25519 AAAA... alex@company
  - If needed, enable serial console for break-glass, add key, then disable after.

- Azure VM
  - Run: az vm user update -g <rg> -n <vm> -u alex --ssh-key-value "ssh-ed25519 AAAA... alex@company"
  - Or use “Reset SSH public key” in the portal.

- On-prem/VMware
  - Use the hypervisor console to add the key to /home/alex/.ssh/authorized_keys (or create the user), then lock SSH to bastion and reload sshd.

Safeguards I will apply
- SSH only from bastion/approved CIDR.
- Key type ed25519, no password auth, no root SSH.
- Short-lived access; disable/remove key at the end of the window.
- If you touched any secrets/keys pre-reimage, we’ll rotate them.

If you can’t get approval in time
- I can pair with you on a screenshare while I run the commands.
- Or the on-call can run commands on your behalf; you provide exact steps.

Please reply with:
- Ticket/approval link and time window.
- Provider + VM identifiers (project/subscription, name/ID, region/zone).
- Your .pub key and fingerprint.
- Whether SSM/OS Login/bastion is available.

Once I have that, I’ll restore your key-based access using the safest applicable method and confirm when you can SSH in.
